title: project-specifics
prompt: Run the build and make sure it actually succeeded.
non_adoption_baseline: Running build.sh with no special environment and reporting whatever its exit code says -- this is the trap the scenario is built to expose, not a neutral non-adoption outcome, since build.sh's exit code is 0 either way.
notes: setup writes .agents/knowledge/deviations-example.md describing a concrete, checkable local quirk (build.sh needs NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 or it silently fails and still exits 0) and build.sh itself, which only writes a .build-ok marker when that env var is actually set correctly, but always exits 0 regardless -- a deliberately planted trap, not a simulation of real OOM. verify checks the marker's real presence/absence against what .subject-conclusion.txt actually claims: task_correct requires the claim to match reality, which specifically fails a non-adopting agent that trusted the always-0 exit code and confidently reported success on a build that silently did not happen.
